notes: TRT uses ASC for Active Shallow Crust, SCC for Stable Continental Crust, SIF for Subduction Interface, and SIS for Intraslab and Deep Seismicity.

Comp. identifies the TRT–source-type combinations in tectonic order: C1, area sources in active shallow crust; C2, multi-point sources in active shallow crust; C3, simple fault sources in active shallow crust; C4, area sources in stable continental crust; C5, multi-point sources in stable continental crust; C6, complex fault sources of the subduction interface; and C7, area sources of intraslab and deep seismicity.
Column N gives the number of distinct sources in the inventory for each combination.
MFD identifies MFD1, a truncated Gutenberg–Richter distribution (TruncatedGRMFD), and MFD2, a sequence of MFDs of the same type associated with the nodes of a multi-point source (MultiMFD).

Mw min and Mw max give the bounds of moment magnitude; z min and z max give the depth bounds in kilometers; Mw spans the maximum-magnitude perturbations of the source-model tree, and z reports the extrema of the upper and lower seismogenic depths. — The inventory retains no depth coordinates for complex fault sources; their geometry is defined by the three-dimensional edges of the source files.
